title: 2008 AMC 8 Problem 17
statement: Ms. Osborne asks each student in her class to draw a rectangle with integer side lengths and a perimeter of \(50\) units. All of her students calculate the area of the rectangle they draw. What is the difference between the largest and smallest possible areas of the rectangles?

solutions.text:
If the side lengths are \(l\) and \(w\), then \(2l+2w=50\), so \(l+w=25\).

The smallest possible area comes from side lengths \(1\) and \(24\), giving area \(24\).

The largest possible area comes from the closest integer pair with sum \(25\), namely \(12\) and \(13\), giving area \(156\).

The difference is \(156-24=132\).

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: A perimeter of \(50\) means the side lengths have sum \(25.\)
For a fixed positive integer sum, the largest product uses numbers as close as possible.
